subject: Re: Pelago private offer — usage bucket reserve & invoice cutover
messages:
From: Alisa Tan <alisa@pelago.com>

Cc: Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@pelago.com>, Pelago Procurement <procurement@pelago.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pelago private offer — request to reserve usage buckets for summer spike

Mina,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the demo helped our CloudOps team validate performance across 16k concurrent sessions. We're close on approvals but have one procurement ask before we can sign the PO: Pelago expects a large seasonal usage spike in July/August driven by a partner campaign. Rather than increasing the total commit, procurement would prefer Redwood to reserve a set of SKU buckets that we can draw from during the spike (so we don't hit throttles or expensive overage pricing).

High level ask: can Redwood allocate a "reserve bucket" of 200k token-equivalents tied to our private offer Sku: RLW-GCP-PLG-001 for July 1–Aug 31? We'd like the reserve to be billed on the monthly invoice as a refundable reserve (if unused, credit back in September).

Attached: an updated internal forecast and the draft invoice cadence we put together.

Questions from our side:
- Are reserve buckets supported on GCP private offers today?
- If not, what workaround can Redwood offer (eg: frontloaded drawdown schedule, committed burst pool)?
- What are the accounting implications for Pelago's procurement team (refund vs. credit)?

Appreciate any quick guidance — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Alisa
Alisa Tan
Head of Business Ops, Pelago Inc

Attachment: Pelago_PO_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal, 1.2MB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alisa Tan <alisa@pelago.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pelago private offer — request to reserve usage buckets for summer spike

Alisa — thanks for the clear ask and the numbers. Short answer: Redwood does not have a first-class GCP "reserve bucket" primitive in the private offer flow today, but we have two practical approaches that meet your procurement and operational needs. I've summarized below with pros/cons and next steps.

Option A — Frontloaded committed drawdown (recommended):
- We accelerate a portion of the committed units onto July's invoice (200k token-equivalents frontloaded).
- If Pelago uses less, we issue a September credit back to your billing account (matching your refundable-reserve request).
- Pros: Minimal engineering change; works within GCP private offer constructs; simple accounting (invoice + credit).
- Cons: Slightly higher upfront cashflow requirement for Pelago; requires explicit invoice schedule.

Option B — Burst pool + rate guard (engineering-assisted):
- Redwood reserves headroom on our dedicated fleet allocated to Pelago and routes burst traffic to that pool. Usage is billed at agreed rate but capped to agreed burst units.
- Pros: No front cash requirement; preserves standard monthly billing cadence.
- Cons: Implementation needs a short routing rule change and operational guardrails; we can commit to this only if we finalize by June 7.

Next steps I propose:
1) If procurement is comfortable with frontload + credit, I will circulate a revised SOW + invoice cadence (Marissa + Finance will prepare).
2) If Pelago prefers burst pool, we need a technical kickoff to scope routing and SLAs; Ben and Laura can lead.

I'll attach a draft invoice cadence and will loop Finance for the credit mechanics.

-Mina
Mina Haddad | Senior Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0119

Attachment: invoice_schedule_q3.csv (CSV: monthly amounts and credit line items)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pelago private offer — request to reserve usage buckets for summer spike

Following up on routing considerations. From an ops perspective, we can stand up a named burst pool and apply a routing policy keyed on Pelago's customer id + Sku (RLW-GCP-PLG-001). Couple of technical notes:
- We can provision the pool with a soft cap of 250k tokens/day for the two-month window.
- We'll apply a rate guard to avoid cross-tenant noisy neighbor impact.
- SLA: best-effort latency parity vs. production; formal SLA requires Dedicated commitment.

If Pelago signs on to test the burst pool approach, engineering needs a signed scope by June 7 to ensure readiness. If they prefer the frontload approach, finance will need the invoice cadence by June 4 to make billing adjustments.

I'll start a short internal ticket with the infra team (JIRA: INF-6423) and ping Laura for runbook entries.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Technical Customer Success | Redwood Inference
